content: Lornoxicam is a member of the oxicam class of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). It exerts its analgesic and antipyretic effects primarily through the non-selective inhibition of cyclo-oxygenase enzymes, COX-1 and COX-2. This medication is commonly prescribed for conditions such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, acute lumbar-sciatica, and for the management of postoperative pain. Lornoxicam is currently available in 31 countries across Europe, the Middle East, the Far East, and South America, and its availability is expanding. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of a single oral dose of lornoxicam in managing acute postoperative pain. Specifically, the study aimed to determine the time to onset of pain relief, the duration before the need for rescue medication, and any associated adverse events. To achieve this, a systematic search was conducted in databases including CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and PubMed up to June 2009. The inclusion criteria for the analysis were randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials that investigated the effects of a single oral dose of lornoxicam in adults experiencing moderate to severe postoperative pain. The methodological quality of the studies was assessed, and data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Pain relief was quantified using the total pain relief score over six hours (TOTPAR 6), and the proportion of participants achieving at least 50% pain relief was calculated. These results were used to determine the relative benefit of lornoxicam compared to placebo, along with the number needed to treat (NNT) for one participant to achieve at least 50% pain relief over six hours. Additional measures included the number of participants requiring rescue medication and the time to its use. Data on adverse events and participant withdrawals were also collected. Three studies, involving a total of 628 participants, met the inclusion criteria. Of these, 434 participants received lornoxicam at doses ranging from 2 mg to 32 mg, 118 participants received a placebo, and 76 participants were treated with other active therapies. All participants had undergone third molar extraction, and the study durations ranged from 8 to 24 hours. For a single 8 mg dose of lornoxicam, the NNT to achieve at least 50% pain relief over six hours was calculated to be 2.9 (with a 95% confidence interval of 2.3 to 4.0). There was insufficient data to analyze the efficacy of other doses or the use of rescue medication. None of the studies reported serious adverse events or participant withdrawals. In conclusion, oral lornoxicam is effective in managing moderate to severe acute postoperative pain based on the limited data available. The incidence of adverse events did not differ significantly between lornoxicam and placebo groups.
